questionText: 1 Cooking fruit and vegetables in water reduces their vitamin C content. The vitamin C is transferred from the fruit and vegetables to the water by diffusion. can be used to estimate the concentration of vitamin C. The blue solution reacts with the vitamin C solution and becomes colourless. You are going to investigate the effect of cooking time on the vitamin C content of the water. Read all the instructions but until you have drawn a table for your results in the space provided in 1(a)(i). You should use the safety equipment provided while you are doing the practical work. Step 1 Label the testtubes 1, 2, and 3. Place the testtubes in the testtube rack. Step 2 Wrap the piece of foil around the beaker containing the piece of citrus fruit, ensuring that the sides of the beaker are covered. Do not cover the top of the beaker. Step 3 Raise your hand when you are ready for hot water to be added to your beaker. The water should cover the piece of citrus fruit. Step 5 After one minute, use the 1cm3 syringe to remove a 1cm3 sample of the liquid from the beaker. Put this sample into testtube 1. Step 6 Wait for one more minute. Step 7 Use the 1cm3 syringe to remove another 1cm3 sample of the liquid from the beaker. Put this sample into testtube 2. Step 8 Repeat steps 6 and 7 with testtube 3. Step 9 Fill the 5cm3 syringe with 5cm3 of the solution. Ensure that there are no air bubbles in the syringe. Step 10 Add one drop of the blue solution to the liquid in testtube 1.
